title: Indian Navy Agniveer SSR Full Length Mock Test 22 (Hard Level)
description: Hard Level Full Length Mock Test for Indian Navy Agniveer SSR. 100 Questions | 60 Minutes | Advanced challenging questions.
instructions: Yeh Hard Level Full Length Mock Test hai.
Har question 1 mark ka hai. Galat jawab par 0.25 marks katenge.
Sabhi sections me qualifying marks lana zaroori hai.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the part with error: Neither the admiral nor the captains was aware of the enemy submarine's position.
options: Neither the admiral nor the captains
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Captains' is plural, so 'were aware' is correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the part with error: The fleet, along with its destroyer escorts, are steaming towards the Persian Gulf.
options: The fleet, along with its destroyer escorts,
questions.explanation: The subject is 'fleet' (singular). 'Along with' does not make the subject plural. Correct: 'is steaming'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the best improvement: The sailors had better to report to the duty officer immediately.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' is followed by the base form of the verb (without 'to'). Correct: 'had better report'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'ABEYANCE': The order for the naval exercise was held in abeyance.
questions.explanation: Abeyance means temporary suspension or inactivity. Synonym: Suspension.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'OBFUSCATE': The commander tried to obfuscate the real reason for the delay.
questions.explanation: Obfuscate means to make unclear or obscure. Antonym: Clarify.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does the idiom 'between the devil and the deep blue sea' mean in a naval context?
options: In a difficult situation with two bad choices
questions.explanation: The idiom means being in a dilemma with two equally undesirable alternatives.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A person who is trained to navigate a ship is called:
questions.explanation: Navigator is the one-word term for a person skilled in planning and directing the course of a ship.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Change to passive: The captain ordered the crew to abandon ship.
options: The crew was ordered to abandon ship by the captain.
The crew were ordered abandon ship.
Ship was ordered to be abandoned.
The crew ordered the captain to abandon ship.
questions.explanation: Correct passive: 'The crew was ordered to abandon ship by the captain.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Convert to indirect: The officer said, "All hands on deck!"
options: The officer ordered all hands on deck.
The officer said that all hands on deck.
The officer asked all hands on deck.
The officer said all hands should be on deck.
questions.explanation: Commands in indirect speech use 'ordered' or 'commanded'. 'The officer ordered all hands on deck.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The destroyer ______ the enemy vessel after a prolonged chase.
questions.explanation: Past tense is required for a completed action: 'intercepted'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The submarine remained ______ for several hours to avoid detection.
questions.explanation: 'Remained' requires an adjective/past participle: 'submerged'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In naval warfare, 'ASW' stands for:
questions.explanation: ASW is the standard abbreviation for Anti-Submarine Warfare.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word related to naval operations:
questions.explanation: In British English (preferred in Indian Navy contexts), 'Manoeuvre' is the correct spelling.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Arrange: P. The aircraft carrier Q. launched its fighter jets R. at dawn S. to intercept the approaching bombers
questions.explanation: Logical order: P-Q-R-S → The aircraft carrier launched its fighter jets at dawn to intercept the approaching bombers.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which sentence logically follows: 'The sonar operator detected an anomaly.'
options: He immediately reported it to the bridge.
The ship was in the harbour.
questions.explanation: The logical continuation in a naval context is reporting the anomaly to the bridge.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The meaning of 'call off' in 'The exercise was called off due to bad weather' is:
questions.explanation: 'Call off' means to cancel.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: ______ the storm warning, the fleet set sail.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is the correct conjunction/preposition here meaning 'in spite of'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The ship is equipped ______ the latest missile systems.
questions.explanation: 'Equipped with' is the correct prepositional phrase.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: By the time the relief ship arrives, the damaged frigate ______ for three days.
questions.explanation: Future perfect continuous is used for an action continuing up to a point in the future.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The torpedo was launched by the submarine. (Active voice)
questions.explanation: Active voice of the given passive sentence is 'The submarine launched the torpedo.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He said, "I am on watch duty tonight."
options: He said that he was on watch duty that night.
He said he is on watch duty tonight.
He said that he is on watch duty.
He told that he was on watch.
questions.explanation: In indirect speech, present continuous becomes past continuous, and 'tonight' becomes 'that night'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the error: Hardly the ship had left the harbour when the storm struck.
questions.explanation: Inversion is required: 'Hardly had the ship left...'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Synonym of 'BELIGERENT' in naval context:
questions.explanation: Belligerent means aggressive or warlike.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Antonym of 'COVERT' operations:
questions.explanation: Covert means secret/hidden. Antonym is overt (open/visible).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The admiral ______ the strategy before the final assault.
questions.explanation: Simple past tense 'revised' fits the context of a completed action before another.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The critical angle for a water-air interface is approximately 48.6°. If a light ray in water strikes the interface at 50°, it will:
questions.explanation: When the angle of incidence in the denser medium exceeds the critical angle, total internal reflection occurs.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A ship's sonar uses a frequency of 40 kHz. The wavelength in water (v = 1500 m/s) is:

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The magnetic declination at a place is 5° West. If a ship's compass shows North, the true North is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic North is 5° West of True North, so True North is 5° East of the compass (magnetic) North.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Why do ships use double-hull construction in cold waters?
options: To reduce heat loss and prevent icing
questions.explanation: Double hull provides insulation, reducing heat transfer and helping prevent ice formation.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Doppler effect is used in naval radars to measure:
questions.explanation: Doppler shift in frequency of reflected waves gives the radial velocity of the target.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Cathodic protection is used on ship hulls. The sacrificial anode is usually made of:
questions.explanation: Zinc and magnesium are more reactive and act as sacrificial anodes to protect the steel hull.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The cetane number of diesel used in naval ships indicates:
questions.explanation: Cetane number measures the ignition quality of diesel fuel (higher = easier ignition).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Desalination on ships is commonly done by:
questions.explanation: Reverse osmosis is the most common modern method for desalination on naval ships.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Divers experience nitrogen narcosis at great depths primarily due to:
questions.explanation: At high pressure, nitrogen dissolves more in blood and affects the nervous system (nitrogen narcosis).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A submarine dives by:
questions.explanation: Flooding ballast tanks increases the weight, making the submarine denser than water so it sinks.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Sonar works on the principle of:
questions.explanation: SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) uses reflection of ultrasonic sound waves.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Naval brass (used in ship propellers) is an alloy of:
questions.explanation: Naval brass is a copper-zinc alloy with a small amount of tin for corrosion resistance in seawater.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: At a depth of 100 m in seawater (density ≈ 1025 kg/m³), the absolute pressure is approximately: (Atmospheric pressure = 10⁵ Pa, g=10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure = ρgh = 1025×10×100 = 1.025×10⁶ Pa. Absolute = gauge + atmospheric ≈ 1.125×10⁶ Pa.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Bioluminescence in deep-sea organisms is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: Bioluminescence serves purposes like attracting prey, communication, or camouflage.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Nuclear-powered submarines use which type of reactor?
questions.explanation: Most nuclear submarines use Pressurized Water Reactors (PWR) for propulsion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Seawater is slightly alkaline with a pH of approximately:
questions.explanation: Average surface seawater pH is around 8.1.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The unit of electrical conductivity used in measuring seawater salinity is:
questions.explanation: Salinity is often measured via electrical conductivity in S/m.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The metacentric height of a ship is related to its:
questions.explanation: Metacentric height (GM) is a measure of the initial stability of a floating vessel.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Rusting of iron on ships is accelerated by:
questions.explanation: Electrolytes like salt water accelerate the electrochemical process of rusting.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Periscopes in submarines use:
questions.explanation: Traditional periscopes use prisms based on total internal reflection.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Decompression sickness (bends) in divers is caused by:
options: Nitrogen bubbles forming in blood on rapid ascent
questions.explanation: Rapid decrease in pressure causes dissolved nitrogen to form bubbles, leading to decompression sickness.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Eddy currents in a ship's steel hull can be reduced by:
options: Laminating the material or using slots
questions.explanation: Lamination or cutting slots increases resistance to eddy current paths.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The gas used in life jackets and inflatable boats is usually:
questions.explanation: CO₂ cartridges are commonly used for rapid inflation of life jackets.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The energy density of diesel fuel used in ships is approximately:
questions.explanation: Diesel has an energy density of about 42–46 MJ/kg.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The speed of sound in seawater is higher than in air primarily because:
questions.explanation: Speed of sound depends on √(B/ρ). Seawater has much higher bulk modulus relative to density.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: If sinθ + cosθ = √2, then the value of tanθ + cotθ is:
questions.explanation: sinθ + cosθ = √2 ⇒ squaring: 1 + sin2θ = 2 ⇒ sin2θ = 1. Then tanθ + cotθ = (sin²+cos²)/(sin cos) = 1/(½ sin2θ) = 2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: If x + 1/x = 3, then x³ + 1/x³ = ?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: A spherical buoy has a diameter of 2 m. The volume of water it displaces when half submerged is: (π=3.14)
questions.explanation: Radius = 1 m. Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³ ≈ 4.186 m³. Half = 2.093 m³.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: A ship travels 120 nautical miles in 4 hours. Its speed in knots is:
questions.explanation: 1 knot = 1 nautical mile per hour. Speed = 120/4 = 30 knots.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: A ship's fuel tank is 60% full. After consuming 1500 litres, it is 40% full. The capacity of the tank is:
questions.explanation: 20% of capacity = 1500 litres ⇒ Capacity = 1500 × 5 = 7500 litres.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: The ratio of length to beam of a frigate is 8:1. If the beam is 15 m, the length is:
questions.explanation: Length = 8 × 15 = 120 m.

questions.question: The angle of depression of a lighthouse from the top of a 50 m cliff is 30°. The distance of the lighthouse from the base of the cliff is: (√3≈1.732)

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: The average speed of a ship for the first 2 hours is 20 knots and for the next 3 hours is 25 knots. The average speed for the entire journey is:
questions.explanation: Total distance = 20×2 + 25×3 = 40+75 = 115 nm. Total time = 5 h. Average = 115/5 = 23 knots.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: If 2x + 3y = 12 and 3x + 2y = 13, then x + y = ?
questions.explanation: Adding both equations: 5x + 5y = 25 ⇒ x + y = 5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: The surface area of a cylindrical fuel tank of radius 2 m and height 5 m (excluding ends) is:
questions.explanation: Lateral surface area = 2πrh = 2π×2×5 = 20π m².

questions.question: A and B can complete a ship maintenance task in 10 and 15 days respectively. Working together, they will complete it in:
questions.explanation: 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6. Together they take 6 days.

questions.question: If the price of diesel increases by 25%, by what percentage should consumption be reduced to keep expenditure the same?

questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)×base×height = (1/2)×8×6 = 24 m².

questions.explanation: (a²+2ab+b²) - (a²-2ab+b²) = 4ab.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: The circumference of a circular radar antenna of radius 7 m is: (π=22/7)

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: A boat takes 3 hours to travel 30 km upstream and 2 hours to travel the same distance downstream. The speed of the boat in still water is:
questions.explanation: Upstream speed = 10 km/h, downstream = 15 km/h. Still water speed = (10+15)/2 = 12.5 km/h.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The motto of the Indian Navy is:
questions.explanation: The motto of the Indian Navy is 'Shaṃ No Varunaḥ' (May the Lord of the Oceans be auspicious unto us).

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: Which is the largest aircraft carrier of the Indian Navy?
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant (IAC-1) is India's first indigenous aircraft carrier and currently the largest.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The first indigenously built nuclear submarine of India is:
questions.explanation: INS Arihant is India's first indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The rank just below Admiral in the Indian Navy is:
questions.explanation: The hierarchy is Admiral → Vice Admiral → Rear Admiral.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar Command is the only ______ command of the Indian Armed Forces.
questions.explanation: ANC is India's only tri-service (Army, Navy, Air Force) theatre command.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: Operation Trident was conducted during which war?
questions.explanation: Operation Trident was a successful naval operation by the Indian Navy during the 1971 war.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The indigenous aircraft carrier INS Vikrant was commissioned in:
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant was commissioned on 2 September 2022.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The missile used by Indian Navy for anti-ship role from ships is:
questions.explanation: BrahMos is the primary supersonic cruise missile used by the Indian Navy for anti-ship and land-attack roles.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Indian Naval Academy is located at:
questions.explanation: Indian Naval Academy (INA) is located at Ezhimala in Kerala.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: Which ship is known as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Indian Navy?
questions.explanation: The first INS Vikrant (R11), decommissioned in 1997, was affectionately called the 'Grand Old Lady'.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The deepest point in the Indian Ocean is:
questions.explanation: The Sunda Trench (Java Trench) is the deepest point in the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Chief of the Naval Staff is a:
questions.explanation: The CNS holds the rank of Admiral, which is a four-star rank.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: INS Kalvari is the first of which class of submarines?
questions.explanation: INS Kalvari is the lead boat of the Kalvari-class (Scorpene-class) conventional submarines.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The highest peacetime gallantry award for the Navy is:
questions.explanation: Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award (equivalent to PVC in wartime).

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Malacca Strait is strategically important because:
options: It is a major shipping route connecting Indian and Pacific Oceans
questions.explanation: Malacca Strait is one of the world's busiest shipping lanes linking the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Western Naval Command is headquartered at:
questions.explanation: WNC HQ is in Mumbai.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: Eastern Naval Command is headquartered at:
questions.explanation: ENC is headquartered at Visakhapatnam.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: Which of the following is a guided missile destroyer of the Indian Navy?
questions.explanation: INS Kolkata is the lead ship of the Kolkata-class stealth guided-missile destroyers.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The term 'Knot' as a unit of speed is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 knot = 1 nautical mile per hour ≈ 1.852 km/h.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Naval War College is located at:
questions.explanation: The Naval War College is located in Goa.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The first Chief of the Naval Staff of independent India was:
questions.explanation: Vice Admiral R.D. Katari was the first Indian Chief of the Naval Staff (1958).

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: Project 75I is related to:
questions.explanation: Project 75I is the programme for building next-generation conventional submarines in India.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Gulf of Mannar is located between:
questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar lies between the southeastern tip of India and the west coast of Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: The Southern Naval Command is headquartered at:
questions.explanation: SNC HQ is in Kochi (Cochin).

questions.subject: GA
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a naval dockyard of the Indian Navy?
questions.explanation: Major naval dockyards are in Mumbai, Visakhapatnam, and Port Blair. Pune is not a naval dockyard.
